ServerProfile.description:
The positive environment/profile capability (LLP 0034 §5 D4 residual,
ENG-22527): auth (`AdminWrite`) answers "may this principal?"; the profile
answers "is this operation appropriate in this environment?". Destructive
and provisioning operations require BOTH. Resolution: `SNAPBACK_PROFILE`
(dev|demo|test|prod) wins; otherwise loopback binds default to `dev` (the
zero-config local posture — OQ7 stands; since ENG-23443 the AdminWrite side
of that posture is a minted token rather than loopback-open) and
non-loopback binds default to `prod`.

@ref LLP 0225#1-ownership-map — deployment-posture vocabulary is leaf-owned;
  environment and bind-address resolution remain in the transport adapter.

description:
The readiness descriptor `snapback start --ready-file <path>` writes once
the listener is bound — the LLP 0030 attach/managed handshake (out-of-band
so `cargo run` launcher noise on stdout cannot corrupt it).

adminTokenFile.description:
Where the serve path persisted its auto-minted admin token
(ENG-23443), when it minted one. Tooling that can read this 0600 file
is already local admin (LLP 0036 D3); a browser page is not.

devIdentityCapabilityFile.description:
Owner-only per-process developer-identity capability on the admin-token
anchor ladder. The descriptor advertises only the resolved path, never
the bearer.

impersonationCapabilityFile.description:
Mechanically derived owner-only per-process impersonation bearer
sibling. Consumers accept this path only when it exactly equals
`<ready-file>.impersonation` and the live startup nonce still matches.

secretReadRootFile.description:
Owner-only root used exclusively by ready-file CLI tooling to produce
one-shot secret-read mint proofs. The descriptor carries only this
mechanically validated sibling path, never the root bytes.

serverProfile.description:
Closed startup posture for lifecycle consumers. Older descriptors omit
it and therefore cannot exercise profile-scoped conveniences.

startupNonce.description:
The writing server's per-process boot id (`/health` →
`binary.startupNonce`). Capability-bearing descriptor consumers use it
as a freshness fence. Lifecycle commands present it through authenticated
`host.stop`; the server compares it with its own boot id and requests its
own shutdown. The descriptor PID is never a CLI signal target; lifecycle
callers bind its OS start time before stop and use only signal-0 existence
observation afterward. Optional only for descriptors written by older
binaries, which lifecycle commands refuse.
